function: Excluded (system): over-the-air aggregation for federated learning (area 7) over a scalar per-subchannel fading link, with no antenna array and no RIS (pp. 3, 4, 14).
notes: Exclusion system. Checks 1 to 5 pass: the work proposes and evaluates TO-OAC and TOR-OAC (p. 2: "We propose an effective trusted online OAC model aggregation algorithm (TO-OAC)"; algorithms on pp. 7-9); the learned element is the model trained across devices through over-the-air computation, which passes no_learning for FL over the air; the problem is the over-the-air aggregation with power control, so the area would be 7 and function does not exclude it. The link is single-antenna with no RIS. p. 3: "We examine a wireless network in which all UEs U can access to a single BS with edge server." p. 4: "Each component of the transmission signal vector is transmitted across orthogonal channels that are segregated by frequency or time", with one scalar coefficient per component (channel vector h_u^t in C^d) and the received signal y^t = sum_u h_u^t o x_u^t + z^t (Eq. 5), with no antenna array or combiner. p. 14: "the channel fading model from UE u to the edge server" is a zero-mean Gaussian per-subchannel fading with path loss and shadowing; Table II lists 500 subchannels of 15 kHz and no antenna count. p. 3 names MIMO only as future work: "massive MIMO [44], and near-field MIMO [45]". No RIS appears anywhere in the text. CAUTION FOR THE REVIEWER: the paper never writes single antenna or SISO, so the single-antenna link is inferred from the scalar per-subchannel channel model and from MIMO being left to future work; confirm this reading on pp. 3, 4 and 14.
